title: Etale schemes over a field and continuous G-sets
statement: Let K be a field [def-pc-field-extension], K^sep a separable closure, and G=Gal(K^sep/K) with its Krull topology. The functor X \mapsto Hom_K(Spec K^sep,X) is an equivalence from the category of etale K-schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism] to the category of discrete continuous G-sets. Under this equivalence, etale coverings correspond to jointly surjective families of G-equivariant maps.

source.place: Tags 03QR (Lemma lemma-sheaves-point), 03QS (Remark remark-covering-surjective), and 03SF (finite etale objects under a Galois extension); the proof uses Morphisms, Lemma 04HF (etale over a field is a coproduct of finite separable spectra)

proof.text: Construct the geometric-point action by precomposition and use [lem-exc-etale-field-geometric-action-continuous] to prove continuity. With the discrete topology these form objects of DiscreteContAction. Postcomposition defines the functor P; its identity, composition and equivariance laws follow from associativity and the Spec functor laws.

Apply [lem-exc-etale-field-point-functor-fully-faithful] and [lem-exc-etale-field-point-functor-ess-surj] to P. These give the Full, Faithful, and EssSurj instances, hence a Functor.IsEquivalence instance and P.asEquivalence. The points equivalences are identity equivalences. Naturality and the specified action formula are definitional for this explicit functor.

By [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], a family covers exactly when it is jointly surjective on underlying scheme points (Mathlib Scheme.ofArrows_mem_smallEtaleTopology_iff). For a covering and a geometric point x, choose a point in some U_i over x(default). Mathlib Scheme.exists_fac_of_etale_of_isSepClosed lifts x through U_i because Ksep is separably closed. This lift is a morphism over Spec K and maps to x. Conversely, Mathlib Scheme.pointSmallEtaleFiberObjToPreimage_surjective supplies a geometric point over every point of X, since Spec K has one point. Surjectivity on geometric points therefore implies joint surjectivity on scheme points. This proves the covering criterion, including arbitrary index universes and the empty family.
